question: Should this PR intentionally reject byte-size config values above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER instead of preserving the previous rounded/fallback behavior for existing oversized configs?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and correct, but OpenClaw policy treats stricter config validation as compatibility-sensitive when existing user configs can start failing or falling back at runtime.

options.title: Accept safe-integer tightening
options.body: Land after fresh exact-head checks, treating unsafe byte-size config values as invalid because they cannot represent an exact byte count.

options.title: Preserve legacy acceptance
options.body: Ask for a compatibility path, doctor warning, or narrowed runtime fallback if existing oversized configs must continue without validation failure.

recommendation.title: Accept safe-integer tightening
recommendation.body: Land after fresh exact-head checks, treating unsafe byte-size config values as invalid because they cannot represent an exact byte count.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared config byte-size helper and are the strongest history match for the config validation contract decision.
